project.name: alquimia-ryan
project.description: Alquimia provides a generic C, C++, and Fortran interface and wrapper library between flow and transport simulators and biogeochemical reaction engines. It delegates geochemical calculations to engines such as CrunchFlow and PFLOTRAN.

nodes.name: alquimia_interface.c
nodes.summary: Creates the generic Alquimia engine interface by selecting the PFLOTRAN, CrunchFlow, or ONNX implementation and wiring its function table at runtime.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses compile-time feature guards and a C function-pointer table to expose one engine-neutral API.

nodes.name: CreateAlquimiaInterface
nodes.summary: Initializes an AlquimiaInterface dispatch table for the requested reaction engine and reports unavailable or invalid engine selections.

nodes.name: crunch_alquimia_interface.h
nodes.summary: Declares the CrunchFlow implementation of the generic Alquimia engine lifecycle, condition processing, reaction stepping, auxiliary output, and metadata hooks.

nodes.name: onnx_alquimia_config.c
nodes.summary: Parses and validates ONNX adapter JSON config, including tensor-to-state mappings, model-path resolution, and named initial conditions, with centralized cleanup on failure.

nodes.name: IsAllowedProperty
nodes.summary: Checks whether a JSON property name appears in the schema field allowlist.

nodes.name: ValidateProperties
nodes.summary: Validates object keys against an allowed schema and reports duplicate or unsupported JSON properties with context.

nodes.name: GetRequiredString
nodes.summary: Reads a required string property from a JSON object and copies it into owned storage with contextual errors.

nodes.name: GetRequiredInteger
nodes.summary: Extracts a required integer-valued JSON property and rejects missing or nonnumeric values.

nodes.name: ResolveModelPath
nodes.summary: Resolves a model filename relative to its config file while preserving absolute paths and allocating the resulting path.

nodes.name: ParseMappings
nodes.summary: Parses an input or output mapping array into owned tensor, feature, and AlquimiaState mapping records.

nodes.name: ValidateUniqueMember
nodes.summary: Rejects duplicate member names inside a JSON object to keep config interpretation deterministic.

nodes.name: ValidateConditionFeature
nodes.summary: Verifies that each condition feature corresponds to a configured ONNX input feature.

nodes.name: ParseConditions
nodes.summary: Parses named initial-condition objects, validates uniqueness and finite values, and stores feature-value pairs in adapter-owned arrays.

nodes.name: ReadConfigjson_contents
nodes.summary: Reads an entire JSON config file into a newly allocated, null-terminated buffer with detailed I/O errors.

nodes.name: PopulateConfig
nodes.summary: Validates the root config object and populates the model path, input mappings, output mappings, and optional conditions.

nodes.name: FreeMappings
nodes.summary: Releases strings and storage owned by an array of ONNX-to-Alquimia mapping records.

nodes.name: OnnxAlquimiaFreeConfig
nodes.summary: Releases every allocation owned by an OnnxAlquimiaConfig and resets the structure to a safe empty state.

nodes.name: OnnxAlquimiaLoadConfig
nodes.summary: Loads, parses, validates, and materializes an ONNX adapter config, rolling back all partial allocations on error.

nodes.name: onnx_alquimia_config.h
nodes.summary: Defines the private ONNX config ownership model for tensor mappings and named initial conditions, plus load and cleanup entry points.

nodes.name: onnx_alquimia_interface.c
nodes.summary: Implements the ONNX Runtime reaction-engine adapter: session and tensor setup, config mapping validation, condition routing, inference, state updates, metadata export, and ordered resource teardown.
nodes.languageNotes: The adapter uses the ONNX Runtime C API with explicit ownership, flattened tensor mappings, and reusable mutable buffers that make a shared engine instance non-thread-safe.

nodes.name: onnx_alquimia_interface.h
nodes.summary: Declares the ONNX implementation of the generic Alquimia setup, shutdown, condition, reaction-step, auxiliary-output, and metadata callbacks.

nodes.name: pflotran_alquimia_interface.h
nodes.summary: Declares the PFLOTRAN implementation of the generic Alquimia engine lifecycle, condition processing, reaction stepping, auxiliary output, and metadata hooks.

nodes.name: alquimia_memory.h
nodes.summary: Declares the allocation and cleanup API for Alquimia vectors, chemistry state, metadata, properties, constraints, and aggregate data structures.
nodes.languageNotes: The declarations are wrapped in extern C guards so the C memory API remains callable from C++ clients.

nodes.name: DriverOutput.c
nodes.summary: Implements pluggable Gnuplot and Python output writers for simulation vectors, including conversion of interleaved multi-component data into per-variable columns.

nodes.name: DriverOutput
nodes.summary: Opaque output strategy object that stores the selected vector-writing function.

nodes.name: GnuplotWrite
nodes.summary: Writes named vectors as aligned numeric columns with a Gnuplot-friendly header.

nodes.name: PythonWrite
nodes.summary: Serializes named vectors as a Python dictionary that analysis scripts can import directly.

nodes.name: DriverOutput_WriteVectors
nodes.summary: Validates vector dimensions, opens the destination file, and dispatches serialization through the configured output strategy.

nodes.name: DriverOutput_WriteMulticompVector
nodes.summary: Deinterleaves a multi-component vector into temporary per-component arrays before passing them to the generic vector writer.

nodes.name: DriverOutput.h
nodes.summary: Defines the public opaque output interface, writer factories, and APIs for exporting ordinary and multi-component simulation vectors.

nodes.name: TransportDriver.c
nodes.summary: Implements a one-dimensional reactive transport driver that parses INI input, manages chemistry-engine state, advances mobile components with finite-volume advection and operator-split reactions, and assembles output fields.
nodes.languageNotes: The C implementation combines an opaque owning struct with an engine function table and explicit allocation and cleanup for per-cell chemistry data.

nodes.name: ParseInput
nodes.summary: Maps INI sections and keys into transport, flow, material, chemistry, boundary-condition, and output settings.

nodes.name: TransportDriverInput_Free
nodes.summary: Releases all optional strings and the enclosing transport-driver input object.

nodes.name: TransportDriver
nodes.summary: Owns simulation parameters, grid state, per-cell chemistry objects, engine metadata, boundary conditions, and advection work arrays for a transport run.

nodes.name: TransportDriver_Free
nodes.summary: Tears down advection buffers, boundary and per-cell chemistry data, metadata, the chemistry engine, and the owning driver.

nodes.name: TransportDriver_Initialize
nodes.summary: Initializes cell properties and chemistry state, applies the initial geochemical condition, and constructs left and right boundary states.

nodes.name: ComputeAdvectiveFluxes
nodes.summary: Computes porosity-weighted primary-component fluxes at boundary and interior interfaces using a first-order upwind finite-volume scheme.

nodes.name: Run_OperatorSplit
nodes.summary: Advances the transport solution through a CFL-limited loop that applies explicit advection, per-cell operator-split reactions, and auxiliary-output updates.

nodes.name: TransportDriver_Run
nodes.summary: Dispatches the simulation to the configured operator-split or globally implicit coupling mode.

nodes.name: TransportDriver_GetSoluteAndAuxData
nodes.summary: Flattens cell locations, geochemical state fields, and auxiliary outputs into named multi-component vectors for downstream serialization.

nodes.name: TransportDriver.h
nodes.summary: Declares transport coupling modes, the complete user-input structure, and the lifecycle, execution, and output APIs for the reactive transport driver.

nodes.name: batch_chem.c
nodes.summary: Command-line entry point that runs a batch geochemistry simulation, selects Python or Gnuplot output, writes final state data, and releases driver resources.

nodes.name: Usage
nodes.summary: Prints batch chemistry command-line usage and exits.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Coordinates input parsing, optional PETSc setup, batch-driver execution, formatted output, cleanup, and process status reporting.

nodes.name: transport.c
nodes.summary: Command-line entry point that configures and runs the reactive transport driver, exports its final solute and auxiliary fields, and performs optional PETSc shutdown.

nodes.name: Usage
nodes.summary: Prints transport-driver command-line usage and exits.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Coordinates input parsing, optional PETSc setup, transport execution, formatted output, cleanup, and process status reporting.

nodes.name: alquimia_util.h
nodes.summary: Declares C-compatible utilities for strings, named-index lookup, deep copying, vector resizing, and diagnostic printing of Alquimia data structures.
nodes.languageNotes: The header wraps its C declarations in extern "C" for C++ interoperability.

nodes.name: BatchChemDriver.c
nodes.summary: Implements the standalone batch chemistry simulation driver, including INI parsing, engine setup, reaction stepping, state-history capture, cleanup, and output-vector assembly.

nodes.name: GetIndexLabel
nodes.summary: Extracts the label enclosed in square brackets from an indexed configuration key.

nodes.name: ParseInput
nodes.summary: Maps batch-simulation INI sections and keys into simulation, material, state, chemistry-engine, and output fields.

nodes.name: BatchChemDriverInput_Free
nodes.summary: Releases dynamically allocated strings and indexed-name arrays owned by a batch driver input object.

nodes.name: BatchChemDriver
nodes.summary: Opaque C driver state holding simulation controls, current geochemical state, engine handles, metadata, initial conditions, and time-history buffers.
nodes.languageNotes: Tree-sitter models this exported C struct as a class-like node; the public header exposes it as an opaque typedef.

nodes.name: BatchChemDriver_Free
nodes.summary: Destroys driver-owned chemistry state, history snapshots, engine resources, metadata, and heap storage.

nodes.name: BatchChemDriver_RecordHistory
nodes.summary: Grows history buffers when needed and appends deep copies of the current chemistry state and auxiliary output.

nodes.name: BatchChemDriver_Initialize
nodes.summary: Transfers configured material and thermodynamic values into engine containers, applies the initial geochemical condition, and records the initial state.

nodes.name: BatchChemDriver_Run
nodes.summary: Advances the batch simulation through operator-split reaction steps, retrieves auxiliary outputs, handles engine errors, and records each completed state.

nodes.name: BatchChemDriver_GetSoluteAndAuxData
nodes.summary: Flattens recorded solute, mineral, sorption, surface, ion-exchange, and auxiliary histories into named output vectors for downstream writers.

nodes.name: BatchChemDriver.h
nodes.summary: Defines batch chemistry input fields and the public lifecycle, execution, and result-retrieval API for the opaque BatchChemDriver.

nodes.name: ini.c
nodes.summary: Implements the embedded inih parser for INI sections, key-value pairs, comments, multiline values, stream callbacks, and file-backed parsing.

nodes.name: ini_parse_stream
nodes.summary: Parses INI content from a reader callback, tracks sections and continuation lines, and reports syntax or handler failures by line number.

nodes.name: ini_parse_file
nodes.summary: Adapts a FILE stream to the generic INI stream parser using fgets.

nodes.name: ini_parse
nodes.summary: Opens an INI file, delegates parsing to the FILE-based adapter, and returns standardized open or parse status codes.

nodes.name: ini.h
nodes.summary: Declares the inih callback interfaces, parse entry points, and compile-time options for multiline input, BOM support, storage, and error handling.

nodes.name: input_util.c
nodes.summary: Implements reusable INI-driven construction and parsing for chemistry engines, regions, states, material properties, geochemical conditions, constraints, and output settings.

nodes.name: ParseEngineData
nodes.summary: Reads chemistry engine name, engine input path, and hands-off mode from an INI chemistry section.

nodes.name: Input_CreateAlquimiaInterface
nodes.summary: Parses engine configuration, creates the selected Alquimia interface, and runs engine setup to populate sizes and supported functionality.

nodes.name: ParseRegionName
nodes.summary: Collects unique region section names into a dynamically resized string vector during an INI scan.

nodes.name: Input_GetRegions
nodes.summary: Scans an input file and returns its declared region names.

nodes.name: ParseRegionCells
nodes.summary: Expands a single cell or colon-delimited range with optional stride into a vector of region cell indices.

nodes.name: ParseRegionData
nodes.summary: Routes region-specific INI sections to state, property, initial-condition, or cell-list parsers.

nodes.name: Input_GetRegionData
nodes.summary: Populates one region's state, properties, initial condition, and cell membership by scanning the input file.

nodes.name: ParseGeochemicalConditions
nodes.summary: Discovers named geochemical-condition sections, grows the condition vector, and parses each contained constraint.

nodes.name: Input_GetGeochemicalConditions
nodes.summary: Scans an input file and loads all named geochemical conditions into a vector.

nodes.name: ParseOutputParameters
nodes.summary: Reads verbosity, output type, and output filename from the INI output section.

nodes.name: Input_GetOutputParameters
nodes.summary: Resolves output options and synthesizes a default gnuplot or Python filename when the input omits one.

nodes.name: Input_IsStateSection
nodes.summary: Recognizes state sections and extracts an optional state identifier.

nodes.name: Input_ParseState
nodes.summary: Parses density, porosity, temperature, and pressure into an Alquimia state while enforcing physical bounds.

nodes.name: Input_IsPropertiesSection
nodes.summary: Recognizes material-property sections and extracts an optional property-set identifier.

nodes.name: Input_ParseProperty
nodes.summary: Parses scalar and species-indexed material properties, validates ranges and identifiers, and writes them into metadata-aligned arrays.

nodes.name: Input_IsGeochemicalConditionSection
nodes.summary: Recognizes named geochemical-condition sections and extracts the condition name.

nodes.name: Input_ParseGeochemicalCondition
nodes.summary: Classifies condition entries as aqueous or mineral constraints, grows the matching vector, and delegates detailed parsing.

nodes.name: Input_ParseAqueousConstraint
nodes.summary: Parses an aqueous constraint expression into primary species, numeric value, constraint type, and optional associated species.

nodes.name: Input_ParseMineralConstraint
nodes.summary: Parses a mineral constraint expression into mineral name, volume fraction, and specific surface area.

nodes.name: input_util.h
nodes.summary: Declares high-level input sweeps and low-level section parsers for engine setup, regions, state, properties, and geochemical constraints.

nodes.name: alquimia_constants.c
nodes.summary: Defines shared string limits, geochemical quantity names, engine identifiers, and error codes used throughout the Alquimia C interface.

nodes.name: alquimia_constants.h
nodes.summary: Declares the public constants for supported engines, geochemical quantities, string limits, and Alquimia error codes.

nodes.name: alquimia_containers.h
nodes.summary: Defines the C-compatible vectors and geochemical state, property, metadata, condition, constraint, and engine-status structures shared with reaction engines and Fortran bindings.

nodes.name: alquimia_interface.h

nodes.languageNotes: A C function-pointer table provides runtime engine polymorphism without exposing engine-specific types to drivers.

nodes.name: CMakeLists.txt
nodes.summary: Defines the core Alquimia library build, conditionally adds PFLOTRAN, CrunchFlow, and ONNX engine sources and dependencies, and installs the library and public headers.

nodes.name: alquimia.c
nodes.summary: Implements process-wide error and abort callbacks plus formatted version reporting for the public C API.

nodes.name: alquimia.h.in
nodes.summary: CMake-configured public header template exposing version flags, engine availability macros, assertions, error callbacks, abort callbacks, and version output.

nodes.name: alquimia_containers.F90
nodes.summary: Defines ISO_C_BINDING-compatible Fortran mirrors of the public Alquimia sizes, state, properties, metadata, status, constraint, and auxiliary-data containers.
nodes.languageNotes: The BIND(C) derived types preserve member order and layout so C and Fortran share the same API containers.

nodes.name: alquimia_fortran_interface_mod.F90
nodes.summary: Provides an object-oriented Fortran facade over the C Alquimia interface, converting stored C function pointers into callable engine procedures and exposing allocation bindings.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses c_f_procpointer to dispatch through a C-compatible function table while presenting type-bound Fortran methods.

nodes.name: c_f_interface_module.F90
nodes.summary: Implements reusable C/Fortran string conversions and a case-insensitive Fortran string comparison used by chemistry-engine adapters.

nodes.name: crunch_alquimia_interface.F90
nodes.summary: Implements the full CrunchFlow-backed Alquimia engine lifecycle, constraint processing, operator-split reaction stepping, metadata extraction, and state translation.
nodes.languageNotes: Wraps module-global CrunchFlow state behind a private engine-state pointer and explicit Alquimia-to-engine packing routines.

nodes.name: crunch_alquimia_wrappers.F90
nodes.summary: Exports stable BIND(C) entry points that forward the generic Alquimia engine operations to the CrunchFlow Fortran module despite compiler-specific module symbol mangling.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: Builds standalone C++/Fortran interoperability experiments for derived types, strings, and pointer-backed structure arrays, with cleanup targets for generated artifacts.

nodes.name: README
nodes.summary: Briefly identifies the mixed-language directory as a sandbox for C and Fortran interface experiments.

nodes.name: cc-f90-strings.F90
nodes.summary: Fortran side of a mixed-language string experiment that reverses a fixed-length C-compatible character buffer.

nodes.name: cc-f90-strings.cc
nodes.summary: C++ driver for testing fixed-buffer string exchange with Fortran, including buffer clearing and invocation of the Fortran reversal routine.

nodes.name: cc-f90-strings.h
nodes.summary: Declares shared constants and the external Fortran string-reversal symbol used by the mixed C++/Fortran example.

nodes.name: struct-array-pointer.F90
nodes.summary: Fortran half of an interoperability experiment that maps a C structure array and nested pointer fields, creates output arrays, and writes results back through C pointers.

nodes.name: struct-array-pointer.cc
nodes.summary: C++ half of a C/Fortran structure-array experiment that allocates nested buffers, invokes Fortran processing, prints results, and frees owned memory.

nodes.name: struct-derived.F90
nodes.summary: Fortran routine used to verify layout compatibility by mutating numeric fields in a derived type passed from C++.

layers.name: Core C API and Runtime
layers.description: Engine-neutral C interfaces, shared geochemical containers, lifecycle helpers, constants, diagnostics, and process-wide error handling form the foundation used by every adapter and driver.

layers.name: Reaction Engine Adapters
layers.description: PFLOTRAN, CrunchFlow, and ONNX implementations translate the generic Alquimia contract into engine setup, reaction stepping, state conversion, metadata, and inference operations.

layers.name: Fortran Bindings
layers.description: ISO_C_BINDING container mirrors, string conversion utilities, and an object-oriented Fortran facade expose the core C contract safely to Fortran callers.

layers.name: Mixed-Language Examples
layers.description: Focused C++ and Fortran experiments demonstrate string exchange, derived-type layout compatibility, and pointer-backed structure-array ownership across the language boundary.

layers.name: Driver Applications
layers.description: Standalone batch-chemistry and reactive-transport programs coordinate input parsing, engine execution, numerical transport, output serialization, and runtime diagnostics.

layers.name: Build and Project Support
layers.description: CMake and Make rules select engine integrations, build and install libraries and drivers, compile interoperability experiments, and preserve third-party licensing terms.

tour.title: Engine-Neutral Overview
tour.description: Begin with the runtime interface factory, the highest-fan-out code entry point in the graph. It shows Alquimia's central design: drivers use one function-table contract while runtime selection connects that contract to PFLOTRAN, CrunchFlow, or ONNX implementations.
tour.languageLesson: In C, a table of function pointers provides runtime polymorphism without requiring C++ classes. Each engine supplies callbacks with the same signatures, so callers remain engine-neutral.

tour.title: Core Data Contract
tour.description: With engine selection established, study the public interface and the memory API on which every adapter and driver depends. The interface defines shared state and callback semantics, while the allocation helpers make ownership and cleanup consistent across dynamically sized geochemical containers.
tour.languageLesson: C APIs often pair opaque or aggregate data contracts with explicit allocation and release functions. This makes ownership visible across C, C++, and Fortran boundaries.

tour.title: Shared Runtime Utilities
tour.description: The constants and utility modules give the contract from Step 2 a common vocabulary and reusable container operations. Their high fan-in reflects their role in error reporting, engine naming, lookup, copying, resizing, and diagnostics throughout the library.

tour.title: Reaction Engine Adapters
tour.description: Next, compare how the three adapters implement the same callback surface selected in Step 1. PFLOTRAN and CrunchFlow translate between Alquimia and native Fortran engine state, while the ONNX adapter manages model sessions, tensor mappings, condition routing, inference, and teardown.
tour.languageLesson: Adapter modules isolate engine-specific state conversion behind one stable callback contract. This allows a driver to switch engines without changing its simulation workflow.

tour.title: ONNX Configuration Path
tour.description: Building on the adapter comparison, follow the ONNX-specific configuration path that turns JSON records into validated tensor-to-state mappings and named conditions. Its explicit ownership structure and centralized failure cleanup prepare safe inputs for the inference lifecycle introduced in Step 4.

tour.title: Fortran Interoperability Layer
tour.description: The Fortran binding layer mirrors the C containers and converts stored C callbacks into callable Fortran procedures. String conversion utilities complete the boundary, allowing Fortran engines and applications to participate in the same data and lifecycle contract from Steps 1-4.
tour.languageLesson: Fortran ISO_C_BINDING supplies interoperable scalar kinds, derived types, and procedure-pointer bridges. BIND(C) layouts and explicit string conversion are essential because native Fortran strings and derived types do not automatically match C representations.

tour.title: Batch Chemistry Driver
tour.description: Now move from library internals to a complete application path. The batch entry point delegates setup, INI parsing, reaction stepping, history capture, cleanup, and result assembly to an opaque driver, demonstrating how a simulator consumes the engine-neutral API.

tour.title: Reactive Transport Driver
tour.description: The transport application extends the same driver pattern with one-dimensional finite-volume advection and operator-split reactions. Read the small command-line entry point beside the driver implementation to see how engine-neutral chemistry is embedded in a coupled transport time loop.
tour.languageLesson: Operator splitting advances transport and reaction as separate substeps. The approach keeps numerical transport independent of the selected geochemical engine while exchanging state through the shared Alquimia containers.

tour.title: Driver Input and Output
tour.description: Both applications rely on shared support for parsing regions, states, properties, conditions, constraints, and output settings. The embedded INI parser supplies low-level key-value callbacks, while the output abstraction converts simulation arrays into Python- or Gnuplot-friendly columns.

tour.title: Interop Experiments
tour.description: The mixed-language sandbox makes the boundary mechanics from Step 6 concrete through small C++ and Fortran experiments. Its Makefile exposes the compile-link relationships for strings, compatible derived types, and pointer-backed structure arrays, making it a useful place to learn or debug interoperability in isolation.
tour.languageLesson: Make targets encode build dependencies, and mixed C++/Fortran targets must use compatible symbol names, data layouts, and linker inputs. Small standalone targets help verify those assumptions before they enter the main library.

tour.title: Build and Packaging
tour.description: Finish with the build definitions that assemble the architecture explored in the preceding steps. The core CMake file conditionally selects engine sources and dependencies, while the driver CMake file links and installs the batch and transport executables against the resulting Alquimia library.
tour.languageLesson: CMake target definitions capture conditional source selection, transitive link dependencies, generated headers, and installation rules. Reading targets from libraries outward to executables mirrors the dependency flow of the codebase.
